name: Rocket 88
artist: Jackie Brenston and his Delta Cats

artist_ref.name: Jackie Brenston and His Delta Cats

podcast.body: Recorded on March 2nd, 1951, and released in late March 1951, "Rocket 88" is often considered by some, particularly producer Sam Phillips, as the first true rock and roll record. The song features distorted bass due to a damaged amplifier speaker cone, a sound that Phillips intentionally kept, contributing to its innovative sound. "But then producer Sam Phillips, a white guy, said, hold on, sounds kind of cool. Let's use it as is."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Recorded on March 3, 1951, this song about an Oldsmobile, performed by Ike Turner and his Kings of Rhythm, is considered by many musicologists to be the first true Rock and Roll record, signifying the "Ground Zero for Rock and Roll." "The song was called Rocket 88, and for many musicologists, that was the first true Rock and Roll record."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 14

podcast.body: Released under this name, the song features a fuzzed-up guitar sound played by Willie Kitsert, resulting from a damaged guitar amplifier where the speaker cone had burst. The band, led by Ike Turner, improvised a repair with wadded newspaper, creating a distinctive sound that some consider the birth of rock and roll due to its early use of guitar distortion. "Now listen carefully, and you can hear the fuzzed up guitar played by Willie Kitsert."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Distortion and Feedback

podcast.body: This song, inspired by the Oldsmobile Rocket 88 car, is frequently cited by many as the first ever rock and roll song. It was recorded in early March 1951 in Memphis under unusual circumstances. "Because of that annoying buzz, the resulting song, which was called Rocket 88 after the Los Mabel, has been called by many the first ever Rock and Rural song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
